purpose: Section 52 — **POSTES ET TELECOMMUNICATIONS**, exercice 2026. Domestic-state share of the section's appropriation.
scope_basis: Whole-section appropriation of a multi-purpose ministry — posts, telecommunications and (to FY2025) ICT. Recorded `partial` under the envelope rule; held for the trajectory and for the named digital projects inside it. Amount is the domestic share only.
doc_locator: Loi de finances n°25/060 du 29 décembre 2025 pour l'exercice 2026, Volume 2, Dépenses, *Synthèse des dépenses par administration*, `SECTION 52`; origin split from *Détails des dépenses par section et rubrique budgétaire*
notes: ⚠ A MACHINERY-OF-GOVERNMENT CHANGE IN FY2026 MOVES THE ICT MANDATE AND ITS MONEY.** The section · names change in the enacted volumes: section 52 goes from *Postes, Télécommunications **et · Nouvelles Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication (PTNTIC)*** to plain ***Postes et · Télécommunications*** — the NTIC mandate is dropped — while section 71 goes from *Numérique* to · Économie numérique***. The money follows: section 52 falls **145,650,630,007 → 55,095,958,006 FC · (−62%)** and section 71 rises **60,627,481,411 → 226,713,223,741 FC (+274%)**. · Neither section's series can be read on its own across FY2025→FY2026**, and any statement about · "the digital ministry's budget" must say which section and which year. Combined, the two sections · are 219,729,663,315 (FY2024) → 206,278,111,418 (FY2025) → 281,809,181,747 (FY2026) FC, i.e. · 0.58% → 0.45% → 0.57% of the total budget** — so the headline jump in section 71 is substantially · a transfer, not new money. · The origin gate is printed in the volume.** The *développement par titre* separates · `Investissements sur Ressources Extérieures`** from **`Investissements sur Ressources Propres`**, · so the domestic share is the state's own disclosure and not an apportionment (driver → *Origin — · the double-counting gate*). The amount recorded here is the **section total less the external · investment group**. · `amount_usd` left blank.** No named fiscal-year-average CDF/USD rate is held, and the driver · forbids spot-converting a fiscal-year figure.
